_comment: Chronos Earth — prehistoric life. Each animal appears on the globe while the timeline is inside its range. lon/lat are a famous MODERN fossil locality; 'track' (filled by scripts/fetch-fauna-paleo.mjs via the GPlates Web Service, MERDITH2021 model) gives that point's reconstructed position at sampled times so the icon rides the drifting continents. fromMa = older bound, toMa = younger bound, in millions of years before present. Add an animal, then re-run: node scripts/fetch-fauna-paleo.mjs

fauna.name: Tyrannosaurus rex
fauna.blurb: The most famous predator of all time — a 12-metre, bone-crushing giant of the very last age of dinosaurs.

fauna.name: Triceratops
fauna.blurb: Three-horned, lorry-sized plant-eater that shared its world (and its fights) with T. rex.

fauna.name: Velociraptor
fauna.blurb: A turkey-sized, feathered hunter — far smaller than the movies, but with a famous sickle claw.

fauna.name: Spinosaurus
fauna.blurb: A sail-backed, river-hunting giant — possibly the longest predatory dinosaur ever.

fauna.name: Brachiosaurus
fauna.blurb: A giraffe-necked giant that browsed the treetops of Jurassic North America.

fauna.name: Stegosaurus
fauna.blurb: Plate-backed plant-eater with a spiked tail — and a brain the size of a lime.

fauna.name: Allosaurus
fauna.blurb: The top predator of the Jurassic — the 'lion' of the Morrison floodplains.

fauna.name: Archaeopteryx
fauna.blurb: The famous 'first bird' — a feathered dinosaur caught mid-way between raptor and bird.

fauna.name: Plateosaurus
fauna.blurb: One of the first big dinosaurs — a Triassic long-neck ancestor walking Pangea.

fauna.name: Coelophysis
fauna.blurb: A slender early hunter from the dawn of the dinosaurs, found by the hundreds at Ghost Ranch.

fauna.name: Ichthyosaurus
fauna.blurb: A dolphin-shaped sea reptile — Mary Anning's famous Jurassic Coast discovery.

fauna.name: Mosasaurus
fauna.blurb: A bus-sized sea lizard that ruled the late Cretaceous oceans.

fauna.name: Pteranodon
fauna.blurb: A 7-metre-wingspan flier that soared over the shallow sea covering central North America.

fauna.name: Megalodon
fauna.blurb: The biggest shark that ever lived — three times the length of a great white.

fauna.name: Titanoboa
fauna.blurb: A 13-metre snake from the steamy world just after the dinosaurs died out.

fauna.name: Basilosaurus
fauna.blurb: An early serpent-like whale — Egypt's 'Valley of the Whales' is full of them.

fauna.name: Paraceratherium
fauna.blurb: The largest land mammal ever — a hornless rhino as tall as a double-decker bus.

fauna.name: Gastornis
fauna.blurb: A two-metre flightless 'terror bird' that stalked the forests after the dinosaurs.

fauna.name: Smilodon
fauna.region: La Brea tar pits, Los Angeles (USA)
fauna.blurb: The sabre-toothed cat — thousands sank into the La Brea tar pits.

fauna.name: Woolly mammoth
fauna.blurb: Ice-age icon of the mammoth steppe — the last ones died out only 4,000 years ago.

fauna.name: Woolly rhinoceros
fauna.blurb: A shaggy two-horned rhino of the ice-age steppe, painted on cave walls by early humans.

fauna.name: Megatherium
fauna.blurb: A ground sloth the size of an elephant, standing tall to browse the treetops.

fauna.name: Glyptodon
fauna.blurb: A car-sized armadillo in a bony shell — early humans may have sheltered inside them.

fauna.name: Lystrosaurus
fauna.blurb: The pig-sized survivor of the Great Dying — for a while, most land animals on Earth were Lystrosaurus.

fauna.name: Cynognathus
fauna.blurb: A dog-jawed cynodont — one of the mammal-like reptiles on the long road to true mammals.

fauna.name: Nothosaurus
fauna.blurb: A sleek, fish-snatching marine reptile that hunted the shallow Triassic seas.

fauna.name: Herrerasaurus
fauna.blurb: One of the very first dinosaurs — a lithe predator from the dawn of the age of dinosaurs.

fauna.name: Postosuchus
fauna.blurb: A crocodile-line apex predator that ruled the land before dinosaurs took over.

fauna.name: Shonisaurus
fauna.blurb: A school-bus-sized ichthyosaur — one of the largest marine reptiles that ever lived.

fauna.name: Diplodocus
fauna.blurb: A 26-metre, whip-tailed giant — one of the longest dinosaurs ever found.

fauna.name: Plesiosaurus
fauna.blurb: The original 'sea monster' — a barrel body, four paddles and a long swan-like neck.

fauna.name: Dilophosaurus
fauna.blurb: A double-crested early predator — far bigger, and far less frilly, than the film version.

fauna.name: Megalosaurus
fauna.blurb: The first dinosaur ever scientifically named, back in 1824.

fauna.name: Ankylosaurus
fauna.blurb: A living tank — armoured head to tail, with a bony club that could shatter bone.

fauna.name: Iguanodon
fauna.blurb: A thumb-spiked plant-eater; one of the first dinosaurs ever discovered.

fauna.name: Quetzalcoatlus
fauna.blurb: A pterosaur the size of a small plane — as tall as a giraffe when standing.

fauna.name: Parasaurolophus
fauna.blurb: A duck-billed dinosaur whose long hollow head-crest may have trumpeted like a horn.

fauna.name: Giganotosaurus
fauna.blurb: A predator even longer than T. rex, prowling Cretaceous South America.

fauna.name: Therizinosaurus
fauna.blurb: A bizarre pot-bellied dinosaur with the longest claws of any animal — up to a metre.

fauna.name: Argentinosaurus
fauna.blurb: Possibly the heaviest land animal ever — a 70-tonne titanosaur.

fauna.name: Uintatherium
fauna.blurb: A rhino-sized browser with six blunt horns and sabre-like tusks.

fauna.name: Andrewsarchus
fauna.blurb: A giant hoofed carnivore with an enormous skull — perhaps the largest meat-eating land mammal.

fauna.name: Eohippus (dawn horse)
fauna.blurb: The 'dawn horse' — a fox-sized forest dweller at the very start of the horse family.

fauna.name: Deinotherium
fauna.blurb: A huge elephant relative with tusks that curved downward from its lower jaw.

fauna.name: Gigantopithecus
fauna.blurb: The largest ape that ever lived — a three-metre cousin of today’s orangutans.

fauna.name: Australopithecus
fauna.blurb: Early upright-walking human ancestors — 'Lucy' was one of these.

fauna.name: Homo erectus
fauna.blurb: The first human ancestor to stand fully upright, tame fire, and spread across the Old World.

fauna.name: Neanderthal
fauna.blurb: Our close cousins — skilled toolmakers and hunters of Ice Age Europe.

fauna.name: Dire wolf
fauna.blurb: A heavier, stronger relative of the grey wolf that hunted Ice Age megafauna.

fauna.name: Irish elk
fauna.blurb: A giant deer with the largest antlers ever — up to 3.6 metres across.

fauna.name: Cave bear
fauna.blurb: A massive Ice Age bear that sheltered — and often died — in caves across Europe.

fauna.name: Carnotaurus
fauna.blurb: A fast, bull-horned hunter from Patagonia, with arms even tinier than T. rex's.

fauna.name: Pachycephalosaurus
fauna.blurb: A two-legged plant-eater with a massively thickened, domed skull.

fauna.name: Edmontosaurus
fauna.blurb: A big duck-billed dinosaur; "mummified" skeletons still carry impressions of its skin.

fauna.name: Maiasaura
fauna.blurb: The "good mother lizard": its Montana nesting grounds show parents caring for their young.

fauna.name: Protoceratops
fauna.blurb: A sheep-sized horned dinosaur of the Gobi, famously found locked in a fight with a Velociraptor.

fauna.name: Oviraptor
fauna.blurb: A beaked, toothless feathered dinosaur. Named "egg thief", but its relatives were later found brooding their own nests.

fauna.name: Deinonychus
fauna.blurb: A sickle-clawed hunter whose discovery in the 1960s recast dinosaurs as active, bird-like animals.

fauna.name: Styracosaurus
fauna.blurb: A horned dinosaur with a crown of long spikes around its frill.

fauna.name: Corythosaurus
fauna.blurb: A duck-bill with a tall hollow crest like a helmet, probably used for booming calls.

fauna.name: Albertosaurus
fauna.blurb: A lighter cousin of T. rex; one bonebed holds over twenty of them, hinting that they lived in groups.

fauna.name: Tarbosaurus
fauna.blurb: Asia's giant tyrannosaur and a close relative of T. rex.

fauna.name: Majungasaurus
fauna.blurb: Madagascar's top predator, with a single horn-like knob on its skull.

fauna.name: Saltasaurus
fauna.blurb: A small sauropod with bony armour in its skin — the first armoured sauropod discovered.

fauna.name: Alamosaurus
fauna.blurb: One of the last giant long-necked dinosaurs of North America, alive until the asteroid struck.

fauna.name: Borealopelta
fauna.blurb: An armoured nodosaur preserved so well that its armour plates and even traces of its skin colour survive.

fauna.name: Carcharodontosaurus
fauna.blurb: The "shark-toothed lizard", a North African giant rivalling T. rex in length.

fauna.name: Ouranosaurus
fauna.blurb: A plant-eater from the Sahara with a tall sail or hump along its back.

fauna.name: Suchomimus
fauna.blurb: A crocodile-snouted fish-eater from the Sahara, a close relative of Baryonyx.

fauna.name: Baryonyx
fauna.blurb: Found in a Surrey clay pit in 1983 with fish scales in its stomach — proof of a fish-eating dinosaur.

fauna.name: Mantellisaurus
fauna.blurb: A lighter relative of Iguanodon, well known from the Isle of Wight.

fauna.name: Utahraptor
fauna.blurb: The largest raptor known — several metres long, with a huge sickle claw on each foot.

fauna.name: Psittacosaurus
fauna.blurb: The "parrot lizard", known from hundreds of skeletons; one preserves long bristles on its tail.

fauna.name: Microraptor
fauna.blurb: A crow-sized dinosaur with feathered wings on both its arms and its legs.

fauna.name: Yutyrannus
fauna.blurb: A nine-metre tyrannosaur covered in long feathery filaments — the largest feathered animal known.

fauna.name: Sinosauropteryx
fauna.blurb: The first dinosaur found with feathers (1996); pigment shows its tail was banded.

fauna.name: Amargasaurus
fauna.blurb: A sauropod with two rows of long spines running down its neck.

fauna.name: Muttaburrasaurus
fauna.blurb: One of Australia's best-known dinosaurs, a large plant-eater with a bulging snout.

fauna.name: Apatosaurus
fauna.blurb: The "deceptive lizard", long confused with Brontosaurus — one of the heaviest animals of the Jurassic.

fauna.name: Camarasaurus
fauna.blurb: The commonest long-necked giant of North America's Jurassic.

fauna.name: Ceratosaurus
fauna.blurb: A Jurassic hunter with a blade-like horn on its nose and a row of bony plates down its back.

fauna.name: Mamenchisaurus
fauna.blurb: A Chinese sauropod with one of the longest necks of any animal that ever lived.

fauna.name: Giraffatitan
fauna.blurb: A towering long-necked giant from Tanzania; its skeleton in Berlin is among the tallest mounted anywhere.

fauna.name: Kentrosaurus
fauna.blurb: A spiky African cousin of Stegosaurus, with long spikes on its hips and tail.

fauna.name: Cryolophosaurus
fauna.blurb: The "frozen crested lizard": a crested Jurassic predator dug out of Antarctica's mountains.

fauna.name: Scelidosaurus
fauna.blurb: An early armoured dinosaur from the Dorset coast, one of the first near-complete dinosaurs ever found.

fauna.name: Heterodontosaurus
fauna.blurb: A small South African dinosaur with three kinds of teeth, including tusks.

fauna.name: Massospondylus
fauna.blurb: An early long-necked plant-eater whose nests hold some of the oldest dinosaur embryos known.

fauna.name: Eoraptor
fauna.blurb: One of the earliest dinosaurs of all, a small two-legged animal from Argentina's Triassic.

fauna.name: Guanlong
fauna.blurb: An early tyrannosaur relative from China, with a thin crest along its snout.
